 Service Academy Clash with Air Force Awaits Women's Basketball on Saturday
 Mids to open their 15-game slate of home contests at Alumni Hall

 ANNAPOLIS, Md. - After opening its 2026-27 campaign with three straight games on the road, the Navy women's basketball team begins a quick three-game homestand on Saturday afternoon with a service academy matchup versus Air Force. Following Saturday's meeting with the Falcons (2-1), the Mids (1-2) will welcome Dickinson College and North Carolina A&T on Monday, Nov. 16 and Friday, Nov. 20, respectively. Navy and Air Force are picking up a series that was active in the 2010's decade with eight meetings, but has only had one matchup since, in Colorado Springs in 2022. Tip-off for the Mids' home opener is set for 1 p.m. at Alumni Hall.
Navy, the preseason Patriot League favorites, is currently on a three-game winning streak when it comes to home opening contests with victories over Longwood ('25), Bryn Athyn ('24) and Susquehanna ('23) during its run. In total, the Mids will play 15 regular season contests at Alumni Hall as part of the 2026-27 slate.
Monday's tip-off between Navy and Dickinson College is slated for 6 p.m.
Navy's two home games this Saturday and Monday will both have live stats provided online, as well as an ESPN+ broadcast.  ESPN+ is a subscription-based streaming service that requires patrons to sign-up for monthly or yearly plans prior to tuning into the contest. 
 Scouting the Competition 
Saturday's matchup is the fourth of the 2026-27 season for both Navy and Air Force ... The Falcons have opened their campaign with three straight games at Clune Arena on the campus of the Air Force Academy and have secured substantial victories over Denver (66-45) and Saint Mary's (61-37) before being tripped up by San Francisco on Wednesday, 77-70  ... During the 2025-26 season, the Falcons posted a 16-19 record with a 7-13 mark in the Mountain West Conference, though they caught fire in the postseason with three straight wins in the conference tournament to earn the program's first-ever berth in the MW Championship Game; they were unable to complete the sweep as they came up short versus Colorado State, 56-42 ... For its efforts, Air Force was selected to participate in the WNIT where it fell in the first round to Northern Colorado by a score of 79-72 ... In the 2026-27 Mountain West Conference Preseason Poll, the Falcons were picked sixth of 10 teams; senior guard Jayda McNabb was noted on the 2026-27 Preseason All-Mountain West Team after averaging 7.9 points and 7.3 rebounds per game with 70 total steals and 28 additional blocked shots.
 Navy vs. Air Force 
The Mids and Falcons have faced off 17 times in a series that dates back to Nov. 22, 1996 ... Since that opening series win by Navy (52-49) at the Gate City Classic in Pocatello, Idaho, the Mids have won 12 of the next 16 meetings to hold an all-time series mark of 13-4 ... Navy is undefeated (8-0) versus Air Force in games played in Annapolis and 4-4 all-time in contests in Colorado Springs ... The two service academy rivals met recently for a stretch of five straight season: 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018 and 2019. During that stretch Navy went 5-0 and outscored Air Force by over 12 points per contest, 64.0 to 52.4 ... They picked up the series in 2022 and the Falcons controlled the Mids with a 90-50 victory in Colorado Springs
    Last Five Meetings (Navy 4 - Air Force 1) 
    Nov. 11, 2022 (A): Air Force 90 - Navy 50
    Nov. 27, 2019 (H): Navy 67 - Air Force 59
    Dec. 7, 2018 (A): Navy 54 - Air Force 47
    Nov. 22, 2017 (H): Navy 71 - Air Force 64
    Nov. 29, 2016 (A): Navy 64 - Air Force 46
 Most Recent Navy-Air Force Matchup: November 11, 2022 in Colorado Springs 
The Navy women's basketball team was knocked off by service academy rival Air Force, 90-50 in a Veterans Day matchup. Taking on an experienced Falcons (2-0) team on their home court at elevation on Friday, the Mids (0-2) were unable to slow down the hosts who shot 65 percent from the floor on their way to a 12-point lead after one quarter of play. At the conclusion of 40 minutes of action at Clune Arena, Air Force was victorious 90-50.
Navy's effort was led by 24 combined points from the freshmen duo of Maren Louridas and Kate Samson . Louridas tallied a team-high 13 points on 6-11 shooting, while Samson went 4-6 from the field and 3-3 from the foul line.
Navy opened the contest off hot as it notched baskets four of the first six times down the court. Mimi Schrader and Samson spearheaded this initial push by the Mids as they each recorded four points. Up 8-5 at the 6:31 mark, Navy's offense was hampered by Air Force's defense and only made one basket over the next five minutes. The Falcons responded to the Mids' cold stretch with a 15-2 run to take a 20-10 lead at 1:52. A Sydne Watts and Gia Pissott free throw rounded out Navy's scoring in the first quarter as Air Force held a 25-13 advantage through 10 minutes of play. As a team, the Falcons shot 64.7 percent (11-17) from the field and 75 percent (3-4) from three-point range to build out their 12-point lead.
The final six-plus minutes of that first quarter played out for the majority of the ensuing quarter as Air Force continued disrupting Navy's offense, while getting points at the opposite end of the court. The Mids struggled throughout the second period and shot just two-of-seven from the field with only Samson and Demos finding the bottom of the basket. Navy's offensive effort was bolstered by five free throws. Holding the Mids to just nine points for the second quarter, the Falcons netted 22 of their own, including 10 off of turnovers to break out to a 47-22 lead at halftime.
Air Force kept its foot on the gas on both offense and defense in the second half as the Falcons netted 25 points and forced eight Midshipmen turnovers, while holding the visitors to 12 points in the third stanza. With the score 72-34 through three quarters, Navy re-gained its shooting form in the fourth as the team shot six-of-eight from the floor, two-of-two from three-point range and four-of-four from the free throw line. Louridas was the catalyst for the Mids' offense as she scored seven of the team's 16 points. Unfortunately, ball-handling continued to be an issue for Navy as it turned over the ball nine times. Air Force used that to its advantage and tallied 18 points in the final frame to close out the 90-50 victory.
For the game, Air Force outshot Navy, 49.3 percent (33-67) to 43.9 (18-41) from the field, 42.9 percent (9-21) to 33.3 (2-6) from three-point range and 88.2 percent (15-17) to 75.0 percent (12-16).
In the rebounding battle, the Falcons out-rebounded the Mids, 35-26 with a significant 17-8 edge in offensive rebounds.
Defensively, Air Force forced Navy into 29 turnovers and was credited with 18 steals. The Mids countered by forcing 13 turnovers on three steals.

 Last Time Out -- Wednesday, November 11 at James Madison in Harrisonburg, Virginia 
The challenging opening stretch of the 2026-27 season continued for the Navy women's basketball team on Wednesday night with a showdown with the James Madison Dukes. Playing at the Dukes' Atlantic United Bank Center, the Mids (1-2) were tasked with taking on a top-flight mid-major program that was picked as preseason favorites for the Sun Belt Conference. Close throughout the majority of the first half, a prolonged slump and 10 offensive rebounds allowed in the third quarter saw the Dukes (2-2) break open the game on their way to a 77-61 victory.
 Zanai Barnett-Gay paced Navy's offense with 16 points on the strength of four three-pointers and a 2-2 showing at the foul line; additionally, she assisted on a team-high four baskets for the Mids. Grace Minihane helped the visitor's cause on Wednesday with a career-high 11 points on 4-5 shooting from the floor with three made free throws. Mary Gibbons had her best offensive game of the young season as she sank a trio of three-pointers for nine total points.
As mentioned above by Taylor, the game opened with a significant James Madison feel to it as the Dukes sprinted out to a 9-1 lead within the first two minutes of play. The hosts later built their lead out to 10, 13-3 by the 6:42 mark of the first quarter. All three of Navy's early points come from the free throw line via successful attempts by Quinn Boettinger , who was making her first collegiate start on Wednesday night. The Mids' defense buckled down for the next two-plus minutes and held the Dukes scoreless, though consequently their offense was only able to shave two points off their deficit during this span. Trailing by eight with 4:40 left in the opening period, Navy whittled JMU's lead down to three at the break as they closed the quarter on a 12-7 run on 5-6 shooting with just one turnover. Two field goals by Barnett-Gay, including a three-pointer highlighted this stretch.
Coming out of the quarter break down 20-17, the Mids tried valiantly to draw even, but every time they cut the Dukes' lead to two, there was a response by the hosts (22-20, 24-22 and 27-25). The first and third times Navy cut it two came courtesy of three-point baskets, first from Gibbons and later from Christina Liggio . Behind by two points at the 4:50 mark, the Mids pulled even closer just over a minute later when Julianna Almeida drove through the lane for a layup to make it a 30-29 game. From that juncture at 3:14 through the remainder of the half and eventually the game, Navy would never be closer. Down 36-31 with the clock showing less than a minute left in the half, Zoe Mesuch splashed home her first three-pointer of the contest. Unfortunately for the Mids, that two-point deficit didn't last long as Ja'quoia Jones-Brown closed the half with jumper in JMU's second-to-last possession to send her team to the locker room at halftime, up 38-34.
That two-possession margin didn't last long coming out in the second half, as the Dukes came out charging and tallied the first five points of the third quarter and grabbed two offensive rebounds to extend their opportunities with the ball. Offensive rebounds and lengthy, successful possessions was the story of the third period as JMU corralled a total of 17 caroms, including 10 on the offensive end on its way to dominating Navy by a score of 21-8 and breaking open a 59-42 lead through 30 minutes of action. Those 10 offensive boards resulted in seven second-chance points for the Dukes in the third quarter. With limited possessions, the Mids were unable to get their offense on track as they shot just 4-12 from the field. Minihane was Navy's leader during this lean time as she was 2-3 from the floor for four of her team's eight points.
Leading by 17 going into the final quarter of play, JMU continued flashing its potent attack and increased its advantage to 26, 71-45 by the 6:06 mark of the fourth. Showcasing the heart of a champion and will to win, Barnett-Gay led a passionate comeback attempt as she rattled off eight straight points for the Mids over a three-minute stretch and later added a three-pointer at the buzzer to tighten the final score to 77-61. In addition to Barnett-Gay's 11 individual points, Navy received five from Minihane and a third three-pointer from Gibbons in the final period of play.
For the game, JMU out-shot Navy, 50.0 percent (33-66) to 39.3 (22-56) from the field, though the Mids held advantages in three-point shooting, 45.0 percent (9-20) to 26.1 (6-23) and in free throw shooting, 66.7 percent (8-12) to 38.5 (5-13).
The Dukes had complete control of the glass as they grabbed 20 more rebounds than the Mids, 46-26; 17 of those caroms came on the offensive end. Lizzie Holder (Sr., Stillwater, Minn.) and Boettinger tied for the Navy team-lead with five rebounds each.
 Parking / Shuttle 
Fans are reminded that the general public does not have access to drive their vehicles on to the U.S. Naval Academy. Fans may park at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium for a fee and take a shuttle that will run every 10 minutes starting one hour before the game and will continue running until one hour after the game is completed. Enter Gate 5 off Taylor Ave. to park at the stadium. Fans 18 and over need a government-issued photo ID. 
**Starting May 7, 2025, in accordance with The Real ID Act of 2005, visitors entering through the Pedestrian Gate 1 Visitor Control Center or accessing the USNA through the fan shuttle bus for a game should be prepared to present a REAL ID-compliant driver's license, U.S. Passport, enhanced state-issued ID, or another acceptable form of identification, to access federal facilities.  Foreign passports are NOT permitted for general access.
